project_requirements.title: What the call wants
project_requirements.question: What must the project address, develop and achieve?

cards.title: Central object
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop?
cards.answer:
A system-level demonstration of an innovative long-duration battery storage concept, storing energy for more than 8 hours, for utility-scale grids or large industrial users.
The technology must not yet be on the market: the call names novel redox flow batteries, high-temperature systems, metal-air systems and multivalent chemistries (organic or aqueous) as examples, but any non-commercialised technology or architecture may qualify.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 105–107 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-05-D2-08, Scope

cards.title: Scope
cards.question: Which activities fall within the funding opportunity's scope?
cards.answer:
Projects are expected to cover all seven points the call lists; the call names no optional or excluded activities.
- Demonstrate an advanced long-duration storage technology not yet on the market
- Assess and define the use cases (front-of-the-meter grid-scale storage, behind-the-meter storage at a large industrial consumer, or firming of renewable generation), with quantified impact on grid resilience, emissions, safety and storage cost
- Assess hybridisation with complementary storage technologies, for example redox flow batteries with supercapacitors, to optimise performance and extend lifetime
- Use abundant, low-cost and sustainable materials with reliable, scalable European supply chains, with realistic pathways to production at scale
- Integrate digital technologies for accurate state-of-charge, state-of-health and lifetime prediction, and optimise battery and energy management systems
- Carry out a techno-economic analysis of capital and operating costs, based on measured performance (self-discharge, calendar and cycle life, round-trip efficiency, safety investments), against the incumbent commercial technology
- Carry out a system-level safety assessment (flammability, toxicity, explosion potential) with mitigation strategies
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 105–107 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-05-D2-08, Scope

cards.title: Problem
cards.question: What type of problem or need must justify the project, and where must it originate?
cards.answer:
Europe needs long-duration storage for grid stability and flexibility that does not depend on critical raw materials.
The need originates with the energy system and its users: grid operators and industrial consumers need storage lasting longer than today's lithium-ion batteries to support energy security, firm renewable output and resilience, while Europe wants to reduce dependence on imported critical raw materials. The call also points to the need for reliable operating data to support an EU-wide stationary storage strategy.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 105–107 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-05-D2-08, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: Deliverables
cards.question: Which concrete outputs must the project produce?
cards.answer:
A demonstrated long-duration storage system, defined use cases, measured operating data, a techno-economic analysis, a safety assessment and an exploitation plan.
- A system-level demonstration of the storage technology
- Use-case definitions with quantified impacts
- A hybridisation assessment
- Digital tools for state of charge, state of health and lifetime prediction, and optimised management systems
- Sufficient, reproducible operating data for detailed techno-economic analysis
- The techno-economic analysis and the system-level safety assessment
- Pathways to production at scale and, for exploitation, preliminary plans for scalability, commercialisation and deployment
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 105–107 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-05-D2-08, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: Impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer:
Projects must contribute to all four outcomes: demonstrated long-duration storage for grid stability, less dependence on critical raw materials, input to an EU storage strategy, and reliable operating data.
- Demonstrated system-level long-duration storage explicitly aimed at grid stability, resilience and flexibility in Europe
- A substantial reduction of Europe's dependence on critical raw materials
- Strategic insights for a coherent EU-wide stationary storage deployment strategy
- Sufficient and reproducible operating data for reliable techno-economic analysis
The call sets no numerical targets, but requires the use cases to quantify impact on grid resilience, emissions, safety and cost.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 105–107 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-05-D2-08, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: After the project
cards.question: How must the result be replicated, taken up and kept in use after the project?
cards.answer:
The results must be prepared for market uptake, with a production route at scale and preliminary deployment plans.
- Where exploitation means a product or service, the exploitation plan must include a strategy and preliminary plans for scalability, commercialisation and deployment (feasibility study, business plan), naming possible funding such as the Innovation Fund (the EU's fund for large-scale clean technology deployment)
- Realistic pathways to production at scale with European supply chains
- The Safe and Sustainable by Design framework (an EU framework for assessing safety and sustainability of chemicals and materials) should be used as reference
- Projects must report results to the European Partnership on Batteries (Batt4EU, a public-private partnership) to monitor its indicators
- The granting authority may object, for up to 4 years after the project, to a transfer of ownership or exclusive licensing of results
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 105–107 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-05-D2-08, Specific conditions and Scope

cards.title: Number of partners
cards.question: What is the permitted or required consortium size?
cards.answer:
At least three independent organisations from three different countries; the call sets no maximum.
The general rule requires, as beneficiaries (organisations that sign the grant agreement and receive funding), three legal entities independent of each other: at least one established in an EU Member State and two others each in a different Member State or country associated with Horizon Europe (non-EU countries taking part in the programme, such as Norway, Switzerland or the United Kingdom). Affiliated entities (organisations legally linked to a beneficiary) and associated partners (organisations taking part without funding) do not count towards this minimum.
The European Commission's Joint Research Centre (JRC) may join the selected consortium, but does not count for the proposal since it does not take part in preparing it.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · B — Eligibility, Consortium composition
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 105–107 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-05-D2-08

cards.title: Partner composition
cards.question: Which types of partners must the consortium include?
cards.answer:
The call names no required partner types; it invites proposals to consider involving the Joint Research Centre.
The JRC (the European Commission's in-house science service) could carry out experimental or desk research on battery performance or safety, joining after selection as a beneficiary with zero funding or as an associated partner. Entities established in an eligible country but directly or indirectly controlled by China or by a legal entity established in China are not eligible, and legal entities established in China are excluded from this destination's actions.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 105–107 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-05-D2-08, Specific conditions and Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 109–110 · Destination Sustainable, secure and competitive energy supply

cards.title: Distribution of work
cards.question: How must work and budget be distributed among partners?

cards.title: Coordinator
cards.question: What type of organisation may or must act as lead applicant?
cards.answer:
No type of organisation is prescribed: the beneficiaries choose one of themselves as coordinator.
The coordinator manages and coordinates the project and represents the consortium towards the granting authority (the European Commission or its agency). At submission it must confirm that it has the mandate to act for all applicants.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Coordinator
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents, Submission

project_requirements.title: TenneT's position
project_requirements.question: What is TenneT's position within the consortium?

cards.title: Coordinate
cards.question: Can TenneT apply or coordinate, and under which conditions?
cards.answer:
Formally yes, but a battery technology demonstration is naturally led by the technology developer; TenneT TSO B.V. would more likely host or advise on a grid use case.
Any eligible beneficiary may coordinate, and a Dutch entity is eligible. TenneT must not be controlled by China or a Chinese entity.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 11, 36 · B — Entities eligible for funding; IMPORTANT, Coordinator
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 105–107 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-05-D2-08, Specific conditions

cards.title: Participate
cards.question: Can TenneT take part without receiving funding?
cards.answer:
Yes, as an associated partner, which takes part without funding and bears its own costs.
An associated partner does not sign the grant agreement, cannot charge costs, does not need legal validation and does not count towards the minimum of three beneficiaries from three countries. It must still register in the Participant Register before the application is submitted.
TenneT could, for example, help define the front-of-the-meter grid use case as an associated partner.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 5 · B — Eligibility, Associated partners
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Registration, Consortium roles and Associated partners
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 105–107 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-05-D2-08

cards.title: Receive funding
cards.question: Can TenneT receive funding, and which funding rate or cost rules apply?
cards.answer:
Yes: as a beneficiary TenneT can receive up to 70% of its eligible costs; it must fund the rest itself.
This topic is an innovation action (a project that develops, pilots and demonstrates new or improved solutions close to the market), for which the maximum rate is 70% for organisations other than non-profit legal entities. The grant reimburses costs actually incurred plus a 25% flat rate for indirect costs. The expected EU contribution is around EUR 9.4 million per project, for the whole consortium. The call sets no Dutch national rules.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · G — Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount, Budget categories
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 105–107 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-05-D2-08, Specific conditions

cards.title: TenneT's likely contribution
cards.question: What contribution would make TenneT credible and useful within the project?
cards.answer:
TenneT could define and quantify the grid-scale use case, specifying what services a long-duration battery must deliver for grid stability and congestion relief.
This is our interpretation. TenneT's time-dependent transmission rights contract with battery operator Lion Storage shows how storage can free grid capacity, and its balancing platform ARTeMIS handles prequalification of flexibility providers. TenneT could supply grid data, service requirements and connection conditions, and assess the impact on grid resilience. Hosting a battery itself is less likely, since TenneT as a TSO is generally not the owner of storage assets.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 105–107 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-05-D2-08, Scope

project_requirements.title: Innovation
project_requirements.question: What type of innovation must the project develop?

cards.title: Innovation threshold
cards.question: Must the project produce genuinely new knowledge or technology, or may it integrate and apply existing solutions?
cards.answer:
The technology must be genuinely new: the call requires long-duration storage technologies not yet on the market.
Integration of existing commercial batteries does not qualify. The digital management and hybridisation work may combine existing methods.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 105–107 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-05-D2-08, Scope

cards.title: Innovation object
cards.question: In what must the project innovate?
cards.answer: Mainly technology (storage chemistry and system architecture), combined with digital management systems and a techno-economic business case.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 105–107 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-05-D2-08, Scope

cards.title: Development stages
cards.question: Which development stages must the project cover?
cards.answer: Demonstration at system level, with preparation for production at scale and deployment; not basic research.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 105–107 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-05-D2-08, Scope

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?
cards.answer:
Activities are expected to reach TRL 6–7 by the end of the project and may start at any TRL.
TRL 6 is technology demonstrated in a relevant environment; TRL 7 is a system prototype demonstrated in an operational environment.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 105–107 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-05-D2-08, Specific conditions, Technology Readiness Level
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 15 · B — Technology Readiness Levels

project_requirements.title: Work
project_requirements.question: Which activities or work structure must the project cover?

cards.title: Demonstration
cards.question: Where and under which conditions must the solution be demonstrated?
cards.answer:
A system-level demonstration is required, supporting utility-scale grids or industrial consumers.
The call does not name a site, but TRL 6–7 means a relevant or operational environment, and the techno-economic analysis must rest on measured performance.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 105–107 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-05-D2-08, Scope and Specific conditions

cards.title: Integration
cards.question: How must the activities fit together and with existing systems?
cards.answer:
The storage must work as one system with its battery and energy management systems.
It may be hybridised with complementary storage technologies and must be designed for the chosen grid or industrial use case.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 105–107 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-05-D2-08, Scope

cards.title: Evidence
cards.question: What must the demonstration prove?
cards.answer:
Measured performance data must prove economic viability and safety against the incumbent commercial technology.
- Measured metrics named by the call: self-discharge rate, calendar life, cycle life, round-trip efficiency and necessary safety investments
- Capital and operating cost assessments based on those measurements
- Quantified impacts of the use case on grid resilience, emissions, safety and storage cost
- Sufficient and reproducible operating data for detailed techno-economic analysis
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 105–107 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-05-D2-08, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: User participation
cards.question: How must users take part in the project?

cards.title: Safety and cybersecurity
cards.question: Which safety, cybersecurity or data requirements must the project meet?
cards.answer:
A full system-level safety assessment is mandatory; the call sets no cybersecurity requirement.
- Safety: document flammability, toxicity and explosion risks and mitigation strategies ahead of wide adoption, using the Safe and Sustainable by Design framework as reference
- Control restriction: entities controlled by China or a Chinese legal entity are not eligible
- Satellite data: if used, Copernicus and/or Galileo/EGNOS must be used
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 105–107 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-05-D2-08, Specific conditions and Scope

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
About 2 projects of around EUR 9.4 million each are expected, within a topic budget of EUR 18.8 million.
- Total project size: not stated
- Grant request: around EUR 9.4 million per project, for the whole consortium; other amounts may be requested and selected
- Funding form: actual-cost grant (reimburses eligible costs actually incurred) with a 25% flat rate for indirect costs
Final budgets may change by up to 20% after evaluation.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 44–45 · Call BATTERIES and ENERGY (HORIZON-CL5-2027-05), Overview of this call
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 105–107 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-05-D2-08, Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 29, 31 · F — Budget flexibility; G — Form of grant

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
Companies such as TenneT receive at most 70% of eligible costs; non-profit legal entities receive up to 100%.
- For-profit organisations: up to 70% of eligible costs, so at least 30% must come from their own resources
- Non-profit legal entities (for example universities and research organisations): up to 100% of eligible costs
- Co-financing conditions: the call sets no rule on cash or in-kind co-financing beyond the funding rate; the remainder is simply not reimbursed
Grants may not produce a profit: any surplus of revenue plus grant over costs is deducted from the final grant.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · G — Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
The grant reimburses only eligible costs actually incurred, plus a flat 25% for indirect costs; subcontracting should stay a limited part.
- Eligible costs: personnel, subcontracting and purchase costs (equipment, travel, other goods and services), plus personnel unit costs where the beneficiary uses them
- Overheads and VAT: indirect costs are a flat rate of 25% of eligible direct costs, excluding subcontracting and financial support to third parties
- Subcontracting or equipment: subcontracting should normally be a limited part of the project and be done by third parties, not by beneficiaries; purchases must give best value for money
Budgeted costs are not paid as such: only the costs actually incurred are reimbursed.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · G — Form of grant, Budget categories and cost eligibility rules
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Consortium roles

cards.title: Cash flow and financial exposure
cards.answer:
Partners normally receive a large advance after signing, minus a 5–8% contribution to a shared insurance fund, then interim payments.
- Payment model: pre-financing (an advance) of normally 160% of the average EU funding per reporting period, then interim payments linked to periodic reports, and a final payment after the final report fixes the grant
- Retention or guarantee: 5% to 8% of the maximum grant is deducted from the pre-financing and paid into the mutual insurance mechanism (a fund covering sums that cannot be recovered from beneficiaries)
- Financial reporting or audit: depending on grant size and type of beneficiary, a certificate on the financial statements may be required; each beneficiary is liable only for its own debts
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 32–33 · G — Reporting & payment arrangements, Certificates, Liability regime for recoveries

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
One stage: full proposals are due by 15 September 2027, 17:00 Brussels time, through the EU Funding & Tenders Portal.
- Stage 1 — Full proposal: 15 September 2027, 17:00 Brussels time; Part A online and Part B of at most 40 pages
- Opening: 5 May 2027
- Additional procedure: none; the Commission may open the call up to one month earlier or later and delay the deadline by up to two months
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 44–45 · Call BATTERIES and ENERGY (HORIZON-CL5-2027-05), Overview of this call
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 3–4 · A — Admissibility, Page limits

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
The call sets no duration or start date: both are fixed in the grant agreement.
- Maximum duration: not set by the call; the grant agreement states the duration in months, and extensions are possible only exceptionally
- Required start: normally after the grant agreement is signed; an earlier start is possible only exceptionally, for duly justified reasons and with the granting authority's agreement
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 30–31 · G — Starting date & project duration

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
Indicatively, the evaluation result comes about 5 months after the deadline and the grant agreement is signed about 8 months after it.
- Funding decision: about 5 months after the deadline (indicative), around February 2028
- Grant agreement: about 8 months after the deadline (indicative)
- Conditions before starting: an invitation to grant preparation is not yet a funding commitment, since legal entity validation, financial capacity and exclusion checks follow; the partners must sign a written consortium agreement
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 30 · F — Indicative timetable for evaluation and for signature of the grant agreement

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
The proposal must be complete, submitted electronically before the deadline, and within the page limit; incomplete applications are rejected.
- Application form: Part A (administrative data and a summary budget, filled in online) and Part B (the technical description, uploaded as a PDF) through the EU Funding & Tenders Portal, using the forms inside the submission system; Part B is limited to 40 pages
- Budget: the summary budget in Part A
- Mandatory annexes: a plan for the exploitation and dissemination of results, including communication activities, and the ethics self-assessment
- Partner documents: the coordinator confirms at submission that it has the mandate to act for all applicants; every participant signs a declaration of honour before the grant is signed
- Registration: every beneficiary, affiliated entity and associated partner needs a participant identification code (PIC, a number from the EU Participant Register) before submission; validation of beneficiaries follows at grant preparation
- Parallel submission: none
- Exploitation plan: for a product or service, preliminary plans for scalability, commercialisation and deployment, naming possible funding sources
cards.sources:

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Independent experts score three criteria out of 5; a proposal needs 3 on each and 10 in total, and Impact weighs 1.5 times in the ranking.
- Evaluation criteria: Excellence (clear, ambitious objectives beyond the state of the art; sound methodology), Impact (credible pathways to the expected outcomes; dissemination and exploitation measures) and Quality and efficiency of the implementation (work plan, risks, resources, capacity of each partner)
- Thresholds: at least 3 out of 5 for each criterion and 10 out of 15 overall
- Weighting: for ranking, the Impact score counts 1.5 times
- Ranking rules: equal scores are separated first by whether a proposal covers aspects of the call not covered by higher-ranked ones, then by the Impact score, then Excellence, then gender balance among lead researchers and geographical diversity
- Budget assessment: the grant awarded may be lower than requested, and topic budgets may change by up to 20% after evaluation
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 23–26 · D — Award criteria, Scores and weighting, Two-stage calls

Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 31 · G — Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
The China restrictions, the possible JRC role and the partnership reporting duty apply in addition to the general rules.
- Exception — entities controlled by China, and entities established in China: not eligible
- Exception — Joint Research Centre: may join after selection as a zero-funding beneficiary or associated partner, without taking part in the proposal
- Conditional — results transfer: the granting authority may object to transfers or exclusive licensing for 4 years after the project
- Conditional — partnership reporting: report results to Batt4EU
- Conditional — satellite data: use Copernicus and/or Galileo/EGNOS if such data are used
- Recommended: use the Safe and Sustainable by Design framework; consider involving the JRC for performance or safety testing
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 105–107 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-05-D2-08, Specific conditions and Scope
